definition: Applying machine learning (ML) (including deep learning) methods to the study of quantum systems is an emergent area of physics research.
details: A basic example of this is quantum state tomography, where a quantum state is learned from measurement. Other examples include learning Hamiltonians,, detecting phase transition in spin-systems even when not trained on physical configurations near criticality, learning quantum phase transitions, and automatically generating new quantum experiments. ML is effective at processing large amounts of experimental or calculated data in order to characterize an unknown quantum system, making its application useful in contexts including quantum information theory, quantum technology development, and computational materials design. In this context, for example, it can be used as a tool to interpolate pre-calculated interatomic potentials, or directly solving the Schrödinger equation with a variational method.

explainer.lead: Applying machine learning, including deep learning, to quantum systems is an emergent area of physics research. It is effective at processing large amounts of experimental or calculated data to characterize an unknown quantum system.

tiers.eli5: It's like handing a computer lots of measurements from a tiny, hard-to-see system and letting it figure out what the system looks like, instead of a person working it out by hand.
tiers.practitioner: Researchers use ML for tasks such as quantum state tomography, learning Hamiltonians and detecting phase transitions in spin systems. A pitfall is expecting phase transitions to be found only if the model was trained on physical configurations near criticality; the techniques can work when it was not.
tiers.paperLevel: Methods include quantum state tomography, where a quantum state is learned from measurement, as well as learning Hamiltonians, detecting phase transitions in spin systems, learning quantum phase transitions, and automatically generating new quantum experiments. The main cited limit is characterization accuracy for an unknown system.

explainer.example: A quantum state is reconstructed by learning it from measurement data rather than by conventional reconstruction alone, which is the basic example of the approach.
